::: {#def-sample}
#### Sample and random sample

A **sample** of size $n$ is the data $\dsn{x}$
observed on $n$ units drawn from a population (@def-population).
A sample is a **random sample** when the units are chosen by a chance mechanism
such that the observations are
[independent and identically distributed](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/independence.html#def-iid)
draws from the population distribution:

$$X_1, \ldots, X_n \iid\ F,$$

where $F$ is the distribution function of the population distribution.
:::

::: {.remark .notes}
Drawing without replacement from a finite population gives observations that are only approximately independent,
and nearly so when the population is much larger than the sample.
Few real studies draw a perfectly random sample,
so conclusions about the population rest on how well the sampling mechanism
approximates one.
:::
